q: Why is an adductor canal block preferred over a femoral block for knee surgery?
why: Sparing quadriceps strength helps early mobilisation and reduces falls.

q: Which nerve does an adductor canal block mainly target?
why: The saphenous nerve (and nerve to vastus medialis) runs in the canal beside the femoral artery.

q: What should you record when a tourniquet is used?
why: Tourniquet time guides safe limits and links to tourniquet pain and ischaemia.

q: What extra analgesia does the surgeon often give at the end of ACL repair?
o: Dilute local anaesthetic into the joint
why: Intra-articular local anaesthetic adds to the block and simple analgesia.

q: Where are most ACL reconstructions managed?
why: Usually young, fit patients who go home the same day.
